Mali.title: Yenchechi, Kidal and Ingouzma: The FAMa...
Mali.summary: Yenchechi, Kidal and Ingouzma: The FAMa neutralise terrorist targets In a statement issued on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the General Staff of the Armed Forces provided an update on the recent operations carried out by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. . Several terrorist bases and hideouts were successfully destroyed during patrols and precision strikes.

Mali.title: Sikasso: A fake sergeant arrested by the security forces
Mali.summary: Sikasso: A fake sergeant arrested by law enforcement A civilian who presented himself as an army sergeant was arrested in Sikasso by law enforcement. The man was arrested after arousing suspicion. He is currently being questioned to determine the reasons for this identity theft.

Mali.title: Guinea-Mali border: 1,557 gold miners of various nationalities released and taken to Kourémalé
Mali.summary: On Friday, 13 November 2026, the Guinean authorities released 1,557 people of various nationalities who had been arrested at mining sites for illegal gold mining activities, according to a report published on the Facebook page of the Guinean Ministry of Defence. . These individuals, after being tried in Conakry, received a presidential pardon and were then taken on Saturday, 14 November to Kourémalé, a town located on the border between Guinea and Mali.

Burkina Faso.title: Road traffic: “No urgency, no social pressure… can justify putting your life or the lives of others at risk”
Burkina Faso.summary: This is a message from the Burkinabe Minister of Security on the occasion of the commemoration of the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, together with the 18th edition of the National Road Safety Awareness Day.

Burkina Faso.title: Road safety in Burkina Faso: Minister Mahamadou Sana declares an end to tolerance of antisocial behaviour on the roads
Burkina Faso.summary: On the occasion of the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day, celebrated on 15 November 2024, coinciding with the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, the Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, issues a firm call for individual responsibility and collective. His message was made public on Sunday, 15 November, by the Ministry of Security. With the theme “Zero tolerance for anti-social behaviour on the roads”, the government intends to strengthen prevention, checks and enforcement of the law to better protect human lives.

Burkina Faso.title: Road safety in Burkina Faso: Minister Mahamadou Sana calls for 'zero tolerance for antisocial behaviour on the roads'
Burkina Faso.summary: On the occasion of the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day, together with the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims, the Minister of Security, Mahamadou Sana, is calling on road users to be more responsible and to strictly comply with the Highway Code. This year's event is themed "Zero tolerance for antisocial behaviour on the roads" . On 15 November 2026, Burkina Faso will commemorate the 18th National Road Safety Awareness Day (JNSSR).

Niger.title: Thousands of Arab Nomads Ordered to Leave Niger
Niger.summary: Several thousand Arab nomads from the Mahamid tribe, who have lived for decades in southeastern Niger, have been told to leave the country by the end of the year, local authorities said Sunday. Niger’s military regime has accused the Mahamid of supplying weapons and logistics to Boko Haram terrorists active in the region. “This is a very firm directive from the country’s highest authorities: the Mahamid must return home by December 31, 2026 — a strict deadline,” a senior official in Niger’s Diffa region told AFP.

Niger.title: Niger: At least 30 civilians killed by "armed men" in the west, according to local sources cited by AFP
Niger.summary: Niger: At least 30 civilians killed by 'armed men' in the west, according to local sources cited by AFP Published on: Advertisement At least 30 civilians were killed on 12 November 2026 in an ambush by unidentified 'armed men' near Téra, in western Niger, close to Burkina Faso and Mali, AFP learned on Friday from local sources. . The attack targeted residents of the village of Tillim, "very close to Téra, killing 37 people, including women and children", said a resident of the town of Téra.
